# re-cordis

> An unpublished Rust reimplementation of the pinned TypeScript Cordis core for local, long-lived plugin applications with typed services, lifecycle updates, events, scoped resources, and logging.

Current package: re-cordis-core 0.0.0, publish=false, Rust edition 2024, MSRV 1.85.
The API is unstable. Use a path dependency on a local checkout, not a presumed crates.io/docs.rs release.
Only re-cordis-core is implemented. Next roadmap targets: re-cordis-timer, re-cordis-logger (console adapter), then re-cordis-loader; other satellites remain candidates.
Targets are not available APIs: review each bounded source/API/dependency scope before implementation.
The semantic baseline is TypeScript Cordis at 35fdc969e4b6c48c48ed44717c7a018324e4dd88, not latest upstream.

This is a documentation retrieval index, not agent permissions or repository policy.
Resolve relative links from the docs/ directory in the same checkout.
Choose English or Vietnamese; do not load both translations unnecessarily.
Exact Rust signatures and bounds come from current source/Rustdoc; older milestone documents describe historical boundaries.

Essential application constraints:
- Drive Runtime::run from a Tokio block_on/main/test entry point. Framework Contexts/handles/futures are local, not a Send/Sync API.
- Runtime owns the host; Context is non-owning. Ordinary spawned Tokio tasks do not inherit framework admission.
- Started operation handles wait for already-started work. Dropping a waiter does not cancel it while the host remains driven.
- Explicitly await cleanup before destroying the runtime. Returning from run is not cleanup; runtime destruction is cancellation.
- Inspect CleanupReport::failures and retained diagnostics. Successful barrier completion does not prove error-free teardown.
- Readiness/update settlement can be Pending. Await provider completion and consumer readiness separately; neither is runtime-wide convergence.
- Failed consumers ignore provider refresh. Explicit update enables recovery; restart does not clear failure.
- Committed injection retains exact provider resources through consumer cleanup. Rc values and BoundService handles alone are not resource leases.
- Service set changes the value, not publication identity, and does not reload consumers.
- Use explicit typed bound calls/accessors/initialization/method injection, not JavaScript Proxy/decorator syntax.
- Enable any extra Tokio features in the application. Example JSON/HTTP/crypto dependencies are dev-only, not framework capabilities.
- GitHub application examples are optional consumers, not permission to log in, send authenticated requests, configure webhooks, or mutate remote state.

- [Plugins and updates](en/guides/plugins-and-updates.md): Validation, source/resolved config, latest-target convergence, explicit recovery.

- [Effects and cleanup](en/guides/effects-and-cleanup.md): Acquisition, composition, rollback, shutdown.
- [Events](en/guides/events.md): Typed dispatch, responder versus around callbacks, snapshots, async timing.
- [Logging](en/guides/logging.md): Scoped exporters, routing, error trees, weak metadata.
- [Testing and troubleshooting](en/guides/testing-and-troubleshooting.md): Common errors and deterministic lifecycle checks.
- [Examples](en/guides/examples.md): Complete lifecycle and bounded GitHub consumers; distinguish offline from live operations.
